name: manual_c317c1
claim:
Meta-record: precise disposition of every legacy lesson connected to the 2026-09-02/03 supersession-scope-and-rendering incident on this same PR (Perpetua-Tools#376), so this whole arc can be traced from a single entry point in the future rather than reconstructed from commit archaeology.

SCOPE, checked precisely rather than assumed: a full timestamp audit of all 240 status="legacy" entries in lessons.jsonl found 228 dated 2026-06-22 through 2026-08-31 -- unrelated, pre-existing entries that predate this incident by weeks to months, out of scope for "what we discovered" here and NOT claimed as rehabilitated by this record. Exactly 12 are dated 2026-09-02/03, genuinely connected to this incident.

Of those 12: 7 are cleanly struck through via a structured supersedes link to their real accepted counterpart (lesson_98de53b747ff, lesson_6cc23d837789, lesson_9a6415ac1a06, lesson_cac6ffb573dc, lesson_7dc92839bb52, lesson_2bfd113c7b78, lesson_40f886e5f5c1). One (lesson_legacy_4c74174d009a) has no supersedes link but renders cleanly anyway, since its actual defect -- a fossilized leading ~~ baked into the stored claim text -- is fixed at the rendering-function source (render_lessons.py's _bullet_for now strips this unconditionally, not just for status=="retracted"), independent of linking. The remaining 3 (lesson_legacy_3a02dcc86148, lesson_legacy_092997ae1643, lesson_legacy_8bf6e1220373) are functionally harmless -- status=="legacy" rows are excluded from recall._load_structured() regardless of linking, confirmed directly by running the function -- but remain visually unlinked in LESSONS.md due to a genuine, checked (not assumed) 1:1 constraint: superseded_by_map() reads exactly one supersedes value per accepted row, and each of these 3 duplicates content whose natural target lesson is already committed to superseding a different legacy id. Not a gap to silently accept: recorded explicitly here as the honest, current state, rather than claiming "all rehabilitated" when 3 of 12 remain a known, understood, low-priority cosmetic limitation.

HOW THIS WAS DISCOVERED: Claude independently patched one specific stray legacy duplicate found while verifying a review-requested supersedes fix. Codex independently traced the actual root cause -- render_lessons.py emitted multi-paragraph JSON claims verbatim into single-line markdown bullets, and ~~...~~ doesn't span markdown paragraph breaks, so the unstruck remainder of a multi-paragraph claim looked like an orphaned new bullet to the legacy-migration scanner and got re-imported as a duplicate on every subsequent render. Running the fixed migration logic against existing data retroactively surfaced 8 more previously-hidden duplicates spanning back to 2026-09-02, confirming the diagnosis rather than assuming it.

HOW IT WAS RESOLVED, in commit order on this same branch: Claude found and fixed one further gap in Codex's own fix (the strip logic only ran for status=="retracted", missing an unsupervised status=="legacy" fossil row) with a RED-then-GREEN-verified regression test. Codex independently split an overly-bundled preservation lesson into three focused, single-topic ones and retired the bundle via a new accepted lesson stating the general principle: when a retrieval system retires a superseded record wholesale, split a broad record before narrowly correcting it. Claude then ran a full timestamp-scoped audit (this record) rather than assuming the earlier partial fix covered everything, finding and linking one more genuinely new duplicate that had appeared in the interim.

Both agents pushed to this same branch independently and concurrently across this whole arc, each fetching and building on the other's latest commit rather than working from a stale local clone -- worth naming explicitly as a demonstrated, working pattern for multi-agent collaboration on a shared branch, not just a lucky outcome.

decisions.notes: Direct request for a traceable meta-record of this whole investigation, with a precise, non-overclaimed answer to whether all legacy lessons are rehabilitated, plus the full discovery-and-resolution narrative for future reference.
